$meta.name: TMT balance defaults (measured corpus heuristics)
$meta.source: TMT-Reference/09-Layer-Design-Patterns.md, §4 Balance heuristics table (measured over 132 published games / 770+ layers); some rows cite §2 patterns P1–P17 for detail
$meta.usage: Use these as DEFAULT numbers when filling the design brief and generating code. The Stage-2 self-check and Stage-6 balance walkthrough verify generated numbers against these ranges. A deviation is allowed only when written down in the design brief with a reason (theme ceiling, idle-first pacing, or scope).

firstMilestone.example: Mario Maker coin milestone 0 at 6871 points vs requires 10

adjacentRowRequiresRatio.evidence: 54 sane samples; anti-pattern A1 = ratio below 1 (The Click Tree 100000→50→30→20→10→5)

prestigeExponentByRow.evidence: corpus histogram: exponent 0.5 in 179 layers, deeper rows drift 0.4→0.1

upgradeCostRatioChained.evidence: 2674 samples; two regimes: gentle 5-upgrade ladders and aggressive row-end jumps

upgradeGrid.idScheme: row-column ids: 11,12,13,14,15,21,... (first upgrade costs ~0–1; last column's final upgrade = 'unlock a new layer' exit ticket)

milestonesPerLayer.densityFloor: at least 3–5 per main layer (anti-pattern A4: thin layers)

milestoneThresholdSpacing.source: 09 §4 row 8; P17 (the threshold number IS the design)

base.note: base 2 = next purchase always ~1 reset away; 5–10 = hard spending decisions

staticLayer.semantic: static layers are 'buy N times' counters; canBuyMax() gated by an upgrade is the standard reward

buyableCostCurve.costSoftcap: optional: blunt late scaling after ~25 purchases (cost-softcap idiom, 01 §7)

softcap.startAt: approximately where the NEXT layer unlocks
softcap.hardCap: power 0 — softcap(value, cap, 0) freezes the value; use for theme ceilings (exam score 150)
softcap.defenseInDepth: three independent places (P12): (1) layer softcap/softcapPower props, (2) softcap() helper inside individual effect()s, (3) staged re-root ladders in custom getResetGain()

automationLadder.crossLayerGrants: layer N's milestones automate layers < N; achievements are an alternate path (P11, with !has guards)
automationLadder.antiPattern: A8 — never one milestone grants everything; one chore removed per step

hotkeyCoverage.rule: every resettable layer gets a hotkey

currencyRetention.rule: each new layer adds at least one gainMult() line to at least TWO older layers, and at least one of its upgrades boosts the FIRST layer
currencyRetention.antiPattern: A7 orphaned first layer; test: 'does layer 1 upgrade 11 still matter at endgame?'

layerDensity.evidence: high-rated games: ~15 (Mining) to ~27 (Mario Maker 2) content items per main layer; low-rated: ~5–7

whenDefaultsMustMove.themeWithNaturalCeilings: hard-cap via softcap(x, cap, 0) and stop that currency's ladder at the cap (Gaokao: exam score 150)
whenDefaultsMustMove.idleFirstAudience: prefer log/custom gains (P8b) over sqrt resets; lengthen the automation ladder
whenDefaultsMustMove.shortGameScope: small tree + dense milestones beats many thin layers (A4)
